title: System Usability Scale
description: Rate your agreement with each statement about teaching the robot this way (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree).

metadata.instrument: System Usability Scale (SUS), 10 items, alternating tone. ADAPTED.
metadata.citation: Brooke, J. (1996). SUS: A 'quick and dirty' usability scale. In P. W. Jordan, B. Thomas, B. A. Weerdmeester, & I. L. McClelland (Eds.), Usability Evaluation in Industry (pp. 189-194). London: Taylor & Francis.

metadata.adaptation: The referent noun is changed from 'the system' to 'this teaching method' throughout, so the scale reads sensibly when the thing being rated is a way of teaching a robot rather than a piece of software. Item order, count, tone alternation, and 5-point response format are unchanged. Substituting the referent is common practice, but the adapted wording is not itself separately validated — report results as SUS adapted from Brooke (1996), not as SUS.
metadata.note: Standard SUS scoring: odd items score (x-1), even items score (5-x); sum x 2.5 gives the 0-100 SUS score. Even items are flagged reverse=true.

items.prompt: I think that I would like to use this teaching method frequently.
I found this teaching method unnecessarily complex.
I thought this teaching method was easy to use.
I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this teaching method.
I found the various functions in this teaching method were well integrated.
I thought there was too much inconsistency in this teaching method.
I would imagine that most people would learn to use this teaching method very quickly.
I found this teaching method very cumbersome to use.
I felt very confident using this teaching method.
I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this teaching method.
